newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania state television sweeps out old guard.
newsitem.headline: Romania state television sweeps out old guard.

text.p: Romanian state television (TVR) on Monday announced a top-level reshuffle, with eight senior news executives replaced by liberal television professionals in the biggest shake-up since the 1989 fall of communism.
"This is the first step towards cutting management jobs in this institution which has scores of managers," a TVR statement said, announcing plans for further sweeping reforms.
The reshuffle had been expected since last month, when the the newly-elected parliament, dominated by centrists, appointed film director Stere Gulea as TVR interim general manager.
The statement said those replaced were sacked because of "the lack of professionalism and credibility" of their programmes, which had lost viewers to burgeoning private broadcasters.
The daily newspaper Libertatea called the move "a tremor rocking state television", the sole nationwide broadcaster which has been plagued with huge debts in recent years.

State television was a powerful propaganda tool under the late Stalinist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu, with daily programmes reduced to a bare two hours of screen time, devoted mainly to Ceausescu himself.

Liberals had repeatedly called for reform of TVR, which they said was subordinated to the former leftist regime of President Ion Iliescu, ousted after seven years in power by the centrists who won last November's elections.
Leftist opposition leaders have criticised the reshuffle, which they said smacked of "a political purge".
